incidents.title: January ascorbic acid stockout
incidents.narrative: Winter Vitamin C demand outran a reorder point set for summer, and Northgate's New Year truck ran ten days late. A Vitamin C batch waited two days for a rush order from Ridgeway Ascorbics with $1,180 of next-day freight.

incidents.title: Mock supplier recall candidate
incidents.narrative: Hollow Pine bought 2,500 kg of ascorbic acid from Ridgeway in one winter order and sent 1,000 kg of the lot to Riverside for its late-winter Vitamin C. The lot went into Vitamin C batches at both plants, so it is the one a mock supplier recall notice traces.

incidents.title: Sierra Mineral Supply ships calcium carbonate late
incidents.narrative: Sierra Mineral Supply's March calcium carbonate arrived nine days after its promised day; the Cal-Mag schedule moved around it and Sierra's on-time rate fell.

incidents.title: Duplicate invoice paid
incidents.narrative: A Pacific Excipient invoice was keyed in twice from paper, the second time with a space and a stray full stop, and both copies were paid. The amount is recoverable.

incidents.title: Fennimore Polyols sorbitol fails QC
incidents.narrative: A Fennimore Polyols sorbitol lot failed the moisture specification. QC rejected it, it went back to Fennimore and a replacement followed a week later; Fennimore's QC pass rate fell.

incidents.title: QuickChem Direct fails two trial lots in a row
incidents.narrative: Hollow Pine trialled QuickChem Direct, the cheapest ascorbic acid on offer. Both trial lots failed assay and went back: two QC rejects in a row, so QuickChem was never qualified. It holds no supplier credential, and RFQ-2611-01 lists it as excluded, vendor not qualified.

incidents.title: Ascorbic acid price hike
incidents.narrative: Northgate and Ridgeway both moved ascorbic acid from $6.40 to $7.10/kg in late August: the list price every order pays from Aug 24, and PO-1042's $7.10/kg.
